question.problem: The points $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ form a triangle. The points $A$ and $B$ are $20\,\text{m}$ apart. If the measure of the angle at the point $B$ is ${47}^{∘}$ and the measure of the angle at the point $C$ is ${62}^{∘},$ how far is point $A$ from point $C?$ Round the answer to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14266767/assets/e9674b5a0921c9fb8d936c435351d0557e90984e4662e9a510a6889812bbad38.png)

The Law of Sines states that

$$
\frac{a}{\operatorname{sin}⁡A}=\frac{b}{\operatorname{sin}⁡B}=\frac{c}{\operatorname{sin}⁡C}.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
m∠B={47}^{∘},\,m∠C={62}^{∘},\,c=20,
$$

and consequently

$$
\frac{b}{\operatorname{sin}⁡{47}^{∘}}=\frac{20}{\operatorname{sin}⁡{62}^{∘}}.
$$

To solve for $b,$ we multiply both sides by $\operatorname{sin}⁡{47}^{∘}$ to give

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡{47}^{∘}\times \frac{b}{\operatorname{sin}⁡{47}^{∘}} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡{47}^{∘}\times \frac{20}{\operatorname{sin}⁡{62}^{∘}} \\ \cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡{47}^{∘}}\times \frac{b}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡{47}^{∘}}} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡{47}^{∘}\times \frac{20}{\operatorname{sin}⁡{62}^{∘}} \\ b & =\operatorname{sin}⁡{47}^{∘}\times \frac{20}{\operatorname{sin}⁡{62}^{∘}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $\operatorname{sin}⁡{47}^{∘}=0.731\,35$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡{62}^{∘}=0.882\,95,$ both rounded to five decimal places to avoid rounding error. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =\operatorname{sin}⁡{47}^{∘}\times \frac{20}{\operatorname{sin}⁡{62}^{∘}} \\  & ≈0.731\,35\times \frac{20}{0.882\,95} \\  & ≈\frac{0.731\,35\times 20}{0.882\,95} \\  & ≈\frac{14.627}{0.882\,95} \\  & ≈16.57,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
